speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a generalized rash; to help me diagnose this, can you tell me exactly when the rash first appeared and if it has spread since then?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-day-old newborn. The newborn was born at term with no complications. The mother had no prenatal care and has a history of gonorrhea treated 4 years ago. The newborn presents with a generalized rash that has been present for 1 day.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Gonococcal Ophthalmia (Ophthalmia Neonatorum) with secondary cutaneous dissemination.

Given the mother's history of gonorrhea and the newborn's age, this is highly suspicious for disseminated gonococcal infection. I need to confirm the presence of purulent eye discharge and check for joint swelling. REQUEST IMAGES: Photographs of the eyes and any joint swelling. REQUEST TEST: Blood_Culture and Cerebrospinal_Fluid_analysis.
